Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: No evidence of business registration integration with a central data exchange. GovStack CMS creates a service catalogue listing administrative services. Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 mentions e-services but no documented business registration exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Both original sources verified: the GovStack URL, despite its 'rwanda' slug, is confirmed by fetching to be GovStack's Somalia country page and is genuinely relevant. Original score of 0 (Unknown) understated available evidence. IFC/World Bank reporting confirms Somalia launched an online business registration and licensing system in March 2022 (extended to Jubaland in 2024), cutting registration times substantially, but no source demonstrates this system exchanges data with tax, regulatory-compliance or other government systems. GovStack's September 2024 assessment states Somalia lacks 'a holistic Government Enterprise Architecture and interoperability platform' and 'enabling legislation for data sharing.' Recoded 0->1 (Not integrated) as this is confirmed non-integration rather than genuine unknown.
revised_comments: Somalia's Ministry of Commerce and Industry operates an online business registration and licensing portal, launched in March 2022 with IFC and World Bank support and extended to Jubaland in 2024, which has substantially cut registration and licensing times. This system operates as a standalone platform: there is no enabling legislation for cross-government data sharing and no whole-of-government interoperability platform in Somalia, so business registration and licensing data are not exchanged with tax, regulatory-compliance or other government systems.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No evidence of electoral register integration with a data exchange system. Somalia is still in the early stages of building its national digital ID which is intended to support future electoral processes.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original LinkedIn source verified as a substantive, citation-backed DPI assessment (December 2025) rather than a weak blog post; it states directly that whether Somali government systems can exchange data remains an open question for 2026-27. Further search confirms the National Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (NIEBC) began digital voter registration in April 2025 using new registration equipment, the first universal-suffrage registration exercise since 1967, but this is a standalone digitisation of the electoral roll with no evidence of integration into a national data exchange or the NIRA digital ID system. Recoded 0->1 (Not integrated).
revised_comments: Somalia's National Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (NIEBC) began digital voter registration in April 2025 using newly acquired registration equipment, marking the country's first universal-suffrage registration exercise since 1967. This is a standalone digitisation of the electoral roll: there is no evidence that voter registration data is exchanged with the national digital ID system (NIRA/HUBIYE) or any other government database, consistent with the wider absence of a national data exchange platform.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No evidence of employment services integration with a data exchange platform.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original LinkedIn source only asserted a general absence of data-exchange integration without addressing employment services specifically. Further search finds Somalia's Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA), with IOM support, launched a National Job Portal / National Employment Service Center on 15 March 2025, hosted on infrastructure of the National Data Agency (Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications), which requires employers to verify business licences before posting vacancies, implying an initial cross-check against business-licensing data. Recoded 0->3 (Under development) given a live but small-scale (under 2,000 registered job seekers as of February 2026) and still-maturing platform.
revised_comments: Somalia's National Employment Service Center, part of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs and supported by the International Organization for Migration, launched a National Job Portal on 15 March 2025, hosted by the National Data Agency under the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications. The portal centralises vacancy postings and job-seeker CVs and requires employers to verify their business licences before posting jobs, indicating an early cross-check against business-registration data. Uptake remains modest, with fewer than 2,000 registered job seekers as of February 2026, and the system is best characterised as under development rather than fully integrated into a broader government data exchange.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No evidence of justice/court system integration with a data exchange platform. Somalia has a fragile state environment with limited government IT infrastructure.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original LinkedIn source predates this development and only asserted general fragility of Somali government IT rather than assessing justice-sector integration specifically. Further search confirms Somalia's Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS) was formally launched on 9 October 2025 (funded by the US Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs, implemented with IDLO), unifying the Criminal Investigation Department, Prosecutor's Office, courts and prisons on a single electronic case-management platform in Mogadishu, with phased national rollout planned. This is direct, verified evidence of operational cross-institutional integration. Recoded 0->4 (Partially integrated), reflecting operational status currently limited to Mogadishu/Benadir with rollout still to reach other regions.
revised_comments: Somalia's Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS), launched on 9 October 2025 with funding from the US Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs and implementation support from IDLO, links the Criminal Investigation Department, the Attorney General's Office, the courts (Supreme Court, Benadir Regional and Appeal Courts) and Mogadishu Central Prison on a single digital platform, replacing a largely paper-based process. Case files, evidence and status information are now shared electronically among these institutions in Mogadishu. The system is being deployed in phases and has not yet been extended nationwide, so integration is partial rather than complete.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: No evidence of driver licensing integration with data exchange systems. Somalia still has limited formal government digital services.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original LinkedIn source predates this development. Further search confirms Somalia's Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation made the NIRA-issued national ID mandatory for driver's licence applications and vehicle registration from June 2025, per a Prime Ministerial Directive of 7 April 2025, becoming the first federal ministry to enforce this ID requirement. This confirms verification-level integration between the driver-licensing process and the national digital ID system, though there is no evidence yet of traffic-offence data being exchanged with other systems. Recoded 0->3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Since June 2025, Somalia's Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation has required applicants to present a NIRA-issued national ID card to obtain a driver's licence or register a vehicle, following an April 2025 Prime Ministerial directive mandating national ID use across government services. The Transport ministry was the first federal body to enforce this requirement, establishing an identity-verification link between licensing and the national digital ID system. There is no evidence yet that traffic-offence records are exchanged with other systems, so integration remains under development rather than complete.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: No evidence of statistics or planning data integration with a central exchange platform. GovStack's Content Management System (CMS) project creates a service catalogue but not a statistics exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original GovStack source addressed a CMS pilot unrelated to statistics integration. Further search of the Somali National Bureau of Statistics (SNBS) confirms it convened a Second Joint Data and Statistics Forum in June 2025 with over 130 government and partner representatives, producing 'improved administrative data-sharing mechanisms' and clearer institutional coordination, and that SNBS operates a MARS platform for SDG data management (per its 2024 annual report). However, SNBS's own 2025 User Satisfaction Survey identifies 'limited data-sharing platforms' as one of the two most-cited barriers (40% of users), confirming integration is real but incomplete. Recoded 0->3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Somalia's National Bureau of Statistics (SNBS) is actively building administrative data-sharing arrangements with line ministries: a June 2025 Joint Data and Statistics Forum, attended by over 130 government and partner representatives, produced improved data-sharing mechanisms and clearer institutional roles, and SNBS operates a MARS platform for SDG indicator management. Full integration is not yet achieved: SNBS's 2025 User Satisfaction Survey identifies limited data-sharing platforms as one of the two most-cited barriers facing data users, indicating the national planning and statistics data-exchange function remains under development.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: No evidence of tax/revenue system integration with a central data exchange platform. Somalia has extremely limited formal tax collection infrastructure. No documented ITAS or equivalent integrated with interoperability systems.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original LinkedIn source did not address the specific state of tax-system integration. Further search finds an active 2025 procurement (RFP, submission deadline extended to 1 March 2025) for the design, supply and implementation of a fit-for-purpose Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS), following a multi-year World Bank-funded design and needs-assessment process. The Office of the Auditor General's January 2025 IT audit of the existing Somali Customs Automated System (SOMCAS) explicitly finds 'a lack of integration between SOMCAS and revenue collection systems,' confirming current systems operate in silos while ITAS integration work is under way. Recoded 0->3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Somalia's tax and customs systems currently operate largely as separate silos: an Office of the Auditor General IT audit published in January 2025 of the Somali Customs Automated System (SOMCAS) found no integration between SOMCAS and the government's other revenue-collection systems. To address this, the Ministry of Finance is procuring a fit-for-purpose Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS), with an implementation contract tendered in early 2025 following several years of World Bank-supported design work. Tax and revenue integration into a central data exchange is therefore under development rather than either absent or complete.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No documented AI integration in government data exchange. GovStack use case implementations focus on high school records and content management system. Somalia ranks 191st on 2024 UN EGDI (score 0.1468). No evidence of AI analytics in any operational data exchange system.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original sources (GovStack, Ecofin) addressed digital transformation generally, not AI specifically. Further search confirms Somalia established a National AI Center (SNAIC) in October 2024 focused on research, education and industry adoption, and a February 2026 analysis states Somalia 'lacks a formal national AI strategy, a dedicated governmental AI agency' and that AI development remains fragmented outside the telecoms sector. No source describes AI applied within a government data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics. Recoded 0->1 (No) — a confirmed absence rather than a genuine unknown, given convergent evidence and the absence of any operational government data exchange for AI to be embedded within.
revised_comments: There is no evidence of artificial intelligence integrated into any Somali government data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics. Somalia established a National AI Center (SNAIC) in October 2024, but its focus is research, education and industry capacity-building rather than embedding AI within government systems. Independent 2026 analysis notes that Somalia lacks a formal national AI strategy or dedicated government AI agency, and that AI activity is concentrated in the private telecommunications sector rather than public administration.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: National multi-stakeholder consultation workshop for Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 involved government, private sector, and development partners. GovStack involves civil society in co-design. Data Protection Authority established. However, Somalia ranks 191st/193 on UN EGDI (2024). Limited public transparency mechanisms for data exchange operations given the nascent state of systems.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Verified both originally cited sources: the govstack.global URL, despite its 'rwanda' slug, is confirmed by fetching to be GovStack's Somalia country page and supports the original narrative. Confirmed the Data Protection Authority is officially operational (launched 24 February 2024 under Data Protection Act No. 5 of 2023), reinforcing the original comment. Found published transparency mechanisms specific to statistics (SNBS Annual Report 2024, published User Satisfaction Surveys) but no public dashboard, published data-sharing agreements or governance reporting specific to a data exchange system — because no operational cross-government data exchange system yet exists to report on. Value Code of 2 (Low - Limited Disclosure) is confirmed as still appropriate; the label 'Low - Limited Disclosure' matches the scale (the em-dash/hyphen variant in Comments is cosmetic).
revised_comments: Public transparency regarding Somalia's nascent data exchange arrangements remains low. There have been genuine public-facing consultations, including a national multi-stakeholder workshop to validate the Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 (October 2025) and GovStack's civil-society co-design process, and a Data Protection Authority has operated since February 2024 under the 2023 Data Protection Act. However, since no operational cross-government data exchange platform yet exists, there are no published data-sharing agreements, no public dashboard, and no dedicated governance reporting on data exchange operations specifically; disclosure is limited to general digital-strategy documents and occasional stakeholder workshops.
